theory.intro: A **frequency table** lists each data value $x$ once, beside its **frequency** $f$ — how many times that value occurs. The same four summary statistics you find from a list can be read from the table without writing the list out: an $fx$ column gives the mean, and a cumulative frequency column gives the median. A **dot plot**, a **frequency histogram** and a **cumulative frequency histogram** are the same table drawn as a picture, so the routines are identical once you have read the frequencies off.
facts: $\Sigma f$ is the **number of data values** and $\Sigma fx$ is their **total**. In a table of pets per household, $\Sigma f$ counts the households and $\Sigma fx$ counts the pets.
$\overline{x} = \dfrac{\Sigma fx}{\Sigma f}$ — build an $fx$ column, add it, then divide by $\Sigma f$.

The **mode** is the data value $x$ with the greatest frequency, not the frequency itself. If every value has the same frequency there is **no mode**; if several values tie for the greatest frequency, report **all** of them.
$\text{Range} = \text{Max} - \text{Min}$, using only the data values whose frequency is **not** $0$.
The **cumulative frequency** (c.f.) of a value is the running total of the frequencies up to and including it.

$\text{Position} = \dfrac{\Sigma f + 1}{2}$ gives the position of the median, and the median is the value whose cumulative frequency first reaches that position. A position such as $13.5$ means the median is the mean of the $13$th and $14$th scores.
The middle row of the $x$ column is **not** the median, and the middle mark on an axis is not the median — the median is the middle of the data values.

On a **cumulative frequency histogram**, each column height is a cumulative frequency, so the frequency of a value is the difference between its column and the one before it. Read the median across from $50\%$ of the total; for ungrouped data the median is simply the score you land on.
steps: Build the $fx$ and cumulative frequency columns

foundation.question_text:
The frequency table shows the number of pets in each of $24$ households.
$\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Pets }(x)&\text{Frequency }(f)\\ \hline 0&3\\ 1&9\\ 2&6\\ 3&4\\ 4&2\end{array}$
Find the mode.
foundation.solution_text:
The greatest frequency is $9$, which belongs to $x = 1$.
$\text{Mode} = 1$

foundation.question_text:
The frequency table shows the number of books each student in a class read last month.
$\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Books }(x)&\text{Frequency }(f)\\ \hline 0&2\\ 1&5\\ 2&8\\ 3&4\\ 4&8\\ 5&3\end{array}$
Find the mode.
foundation.solution_text:
The greatest frequency is $8$, which belongs to $x = 2$ and to $x = 4$.
$\text{Mode} = 2 \text{ and } 4$

foundation.question_text:
The frequency table shows the number of days each of $24$ students was absent last week.
$\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Days absent }(x)&\text{Frequency }(f)\\ \hline 0&6\\ 1&6\\ 2&6\\ 3&6\end{array}$
Find the mode.
foundation.solution_text: Every data value has the same frequency of $6$, so this dataset has no mode.

foundation.question_text:
The frequency table shows the number of goals a team scored in each of $21$ matches.
$\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Goals }(x)&\text{Frequency }(f)\\ \hline 0&0\\ 1&6\\ 2&9\\ 3&4\\ 4&2\\ 5&0\end{array}$
Find the range.
foundation.solution_text:
$x = 0$ and $x = 5$ have frequency $0$, so no match ended with $0$ goals or with $5$ goals.
$\text{Range} = \text{Max} - \text{Min}$
$= 4 - 1$
$= 3$

The frequency table shows the number of books each of $23$ students read last month.
$\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Books }(x)&\text{Frequency }(f)\\ \hline 0&3\\ 1&6\\ 2&8\\ 3&4\\ 4&2\end{array}$

foundation.solution_text:

foundation.question_text:
The frequency table shows the number of days each of $24$ students was absent last week.
$\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Days absent }(x)&\text{Frequency }(f)\\ \hline 0&2\\ 1&4\\ 2&3\\ 3&8\\ 4&5\\ 5&2\end{array}$
Find the median.
foundation.solution_text:
$\begin{array}{c|c|c}x&f&\text{c.f.}\\ \hline 0&2&2\\ 1&4&6\\ 2&3&9\\ 3&8&17\\ 4&5&22\\ 5&2&24\end{array}$
$\text{Position} = \frac{24 + 1}{2}$
$= 12.5$
Scores $10$ to $17$ are all $3$, so the $12$th and $13$th scores are both $3$.
$\text{Median} = 3$

foundation.question_text:
The frequency table shows the number of siblings of each student in a class.
$\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Siblings }(x)&\text{Frequency }(f)\\ \hline 0&6\\ 1&10\\ 2&7\\ 3&4\\ 4&3\end{array}$
How many students are in the class, and how many siblings do they have altogether?
foundation.solution_text:
$\Sigma f = 6 + 10 + 7 + 4 + 3$
$= 30$
$\Sigma fx = (0 \times 6) + (1 \times 10) + (2 \times 7) + (3 \times 4) + (4 \times 3)$
$= 48$
There are $30$ students, and altogether they have $48$ siblings.

development.question_text:
The frequency table shows the number of days each of $26$ students was absent last week.
$\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Days absent }(x)&\text{Frequency }(f)\\ \hline 0&7\\ 1&5\\ 2&9\\ 3&3\\ 4&2\end{array}$
Find the range, mode, median and mean, giving the mean correct to $1$ decimal place.
development.solution_text:
1. **Build the $fx$ and cumulative frequency columns**
$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}x&f&fx&\text{c.f.}\\ \hline 0&7&0&7\\ 1&5&5&12\\ 2&9&18&21\\ 3&3&9&24\\ 4&2&8&26\end{array}$
$\Sigma f = 26$
$\Sigma fx = 40$
2. **Find the range**
$\text{Range} = 4 - 0$
$= 4$
3. **Find the mode**
$\text{Mode} = 2$
4. **Find the median**
$\text{Position} = \frac{26 + 1}{2}$
$= 13.5$
Scores $13$ to $21$ are all $2$, so the $13$th and $14$th scores are both $2$.
$\text{Median} = 2$
5. **Find the mean**
$\overline{x} = \frac{40}{26}$
$\approx 1.5$

Find the mean number of books, correct to $1$ decimal place.
development.solution_text:
Each frequency is the cumulative frequency minus the one before it.
$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}x&\text{c.f.}&f&fx\\ \hline 1&4&4&4\\ 2&11&7&14\\ 3&17&6&18\\ 4&20&3&12\\ 5&22&2&10\end{array}$

$\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Pets }(x)&\text{Frequency }(f)\\ \hline 0&9\\ 1&7\\ 2&5\\ 3&2\\ 4&1\end{array}$
Rohan says the median is $2$, because $2$ is in the middle of $0$, $1$, $2$, $3$ and $4$. Explain why Rohan is wrong, then find the correct median.
development.solution_text:
Rohan has taken the middle of the $x$ column, but the median is the middle of the $24$ data values, and most of those values are $0$ or $1$.
$\begin{array}{c|c|c}x&f&\text{c.f.}\\ \hline 0&9&9\\ 1&7&16\\ 2&5&21\\ 3&2&23\\ 4&1&24\end{array}$
$\text{Position} = \frac{24 + 1}{2}$
$= 12.5$
Scores $10$ to $16$ are all $1$, so the $12$th and $13$th scores are both $1$.
$\text{Median} = 1$

development.solution_text:

mastery.question_text:
The frequency table shows the number of pets in each of $26$ households.
$\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Pets }(x)&\text{Frequency }(f)\\ \hline 0&2\\ 1&5\\ 2&6\\ 3&9\\ 4&4\end{array}$
Find the median and the mean, giving the mean correct to $1$ decimal place.
mastery.solution_text:
$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}x&f&fx&\text{c.f.}\\ \hline 0&2&0&2\\ 1&5&5&7\\ 2&6&12&13\\ 3&9&27&22\\ 4&4&16&26\end{array}$
$\Sigma f = 26$
$\Sigma fx = 60$
$\text{Position} = \frac{26 + 1}{2}$
$= 13.5$
The cumulative frequency reaches exactly $13$ at $x = 2$, so the $13$th score is $2$ and the $14$th score is $3$.
$\text{Median} = \frac{2 + 3}{2}$
$= 2.5$
$\overline{x} = \frac{60}{26}$
$\approx 2.3$
